_note: Single definition point for every ledger record type in this repository.
scripts/ledger_gate.py is the only reader. There is deliberately no second
copy in JSON Schema form: two definitions drift, and only one of them gets
Supported field types: string, integer, number, boolean, array, object,
A field may declare: required, pattern, enum, min_length, items, nullable,
vocabulary (a closed label set loaded from another file).

failure_cause.why: the label set is closed on purpose: free text in a cause field makes recurrence uncountable

prereg.title: pre-registration of a claim, written before the measurement runs

metric_definition_point._why: a path. The metric must be defined in exactly one place, or every arm can quietly use its own

stop_conditions._why: the conditions under which the result is NOT scored. Without these, a failed control gets read as a weak result

controls._why: a claim with no control is not falsifiable

negative_result_is_a_result._why: must be stated before the run, so that a null finding cannot be reframed afterwards as a failed experiment

negative_result.title: a claim that was measured and did not survive

prereg_criteria._why: the pass/fail rule as it was registered, not as it reads in hindsight

measured._why: numbers. 'it did not work' is not a measurement

withdrawn_claim._why: if something was previously asserted and is now retracted, the retracted wording is recorded verbatim

reopen_condition._why: either the evidence that would reopen this, or an explicit statement that nothing will

detected_by._why: which check caught it. 'noticed while reading' is an admission that no check exists

close_predicate._why: the machine condition under which this is closed. Written at open time, not at close time

external_response.title: a response to an issue raised from outside this repository
_defined_but_not_counted: This type exists so that external responses have a schema on the day the
repository is first published. Nothing is counted yet.
It is a SEPARATE instrument. External responses must never be added to the
numerator of the human-intervention rate: that numerator counts occasions on
which the work moved back to a human inside the system's own loop. Answering
someone else's question is not that, and folding the two together would make
the system look worse the more useful it is to other people — which would
create a standing incentive to ignore them.

test_added._why: the path of the test that now covers it, or null with the reason recorded in the outcome
